reader.requirement: At 1985 the implementor must specify any rule for synchronizing the records of a data file as it affects synchronization of elementary items, and the compiler must behave as specified for records written and read in every organization (sequential, relative, indexed) and for variable-length records.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2023 (DialectLevel < 2023) refuses SYNCHRONIZED on a group item (Constructs.SyncOnGroup2023, COBOL0900) per §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1; elementary SYNC takes the same path at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Dialect|Construct in DataBinder.SynchronizedClause.cs: only GateSynchronizedGroup. grep -rn Synchronized over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen and src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime: only RepositoryAttributeRenderer (metadata); no layout, width, offset, file-record or move code reads the flag, so no edition arm exists on the storage path.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the documented rule (no record-level synchronization; a SYNC item sits at its unsynchronized offset) is stated 'the same in every edition' and the code has one path
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf12_02 covers a sequential file with a fixed record; not relative or indexed organizations, a variable-length (RECORD VARYING / OCCURS DEPENDING) record, or SYNC LEFT/RIGHT

probes.printed: REL=YES IDX=YES VL2=05 VAR=YES V-END R9-INV
probes.expected: per DOC-A.1-196: a relative record with S9(4) COMP SYNC reads back as 4 unpadded positions; an indexed record with S9(9) COMP SYNC LEFT round-trips; a RECORD VARYING record with an ODO table of SYNC RIGHT items is 5 positions (no slack) and the next READ is AT END; a READ of a missing relative record takes INVALID KEY

probes.printed: COBOL0900: SYNCHRONIZED on a group item requires COBOL-2023 (targeting COBOL-85)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.13.4 GR10  (5.13.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10
OK  §1985:VI.5.13.3 SR1  (5.13.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The implementor rule is documented (DOC-A.1-196: no record-level synchronization; DOC-A.1-195: no alignment or implicit FILLER), and nothing on the layout or file path reads the SYNCHRONIZED flag, so records are their own unpadded image. DOC-A.1-196 labels the item 'optional (documented if provided)' after the 2023 text, while 1985 GR10 says 'will be specified'; the entry still specifies the rule (none), so the 1985 obligation is met.

refuter.evidence: Read DOC-A.1-196 and DOC-A.1-195. The rule is specified as 'no record-level synchronization; a SYNC item sits at its unsynchronized offset', which meets GR10's 'will be specified by the implementor'. I measured that documented claim directly. Probe sy1.cob (sy1-001) wrote the documented example record (Q, 258 in S9(4) COMP SYNC, Z), and od of sy1.dat gave 51 01 02 5a, exactly as documented. Read back through a PIC X(4) FD over the same file it gave R2-1=Q and R2-4=Z, and the next READ was AT END. A SORT whose SD record has a S9(4) COMP SYNC RIGHT key, GIVING an FD whose item is SYNC LEFT, wrote 12 bytes (62 02 bc 79 63 00 05 7a 61 ff fd 78: 4 per record, no slack), ordered descending on the binary key (700, 5, -3). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.13.4 GR10 (the text is in GR10).
